name: الفئة لتمثيل نقطة في المستوى الإقليدي (الحالة 2)
description: قم ببناء فئة تمثل نقطة في المستوى الإقليدي. يجب أن تحتوي الفئة على بيانات تمثل الإحداثيات الصحيحة للنقطة (x,y). لا يمكن الوصول إلى إحداثيات النقطة أو تغييرها إلا من خلال طرق getter و setter. يجب أن تتضمن الفئة أيضًا طريقة لحساب وإرجاع مسافة النقطة من الأصل (0,0).
code:
#Khatwa 1: Ta'reef al-fasl
class Point2 :
    #Khatwa 1.1: I'lan al-tariqa li-hisab wa 'iidat musaafat al-noqta min al-asl
    def distance_from_origin(self) :
        return (self.__x * self.__x + self.__y * self.__y) ** 0.5
    #Khatwa 1.2: Ta'reef wasa'il al-setter wa al-getter li-iHdaathiyat x lil-noqta
    def set_x(self, new_x) :
        self.__x = new_x
    def get_x(self) :
        return self.__x
    #Khatwa 1.3: Ta'reef wasa'il al-setter wa al-getter li-iHdaathiyat y lil-noqta
    def set_y(self, new_y) :
        self.__y = new_y
    def get_y(self) :
        return self.__y
#Khatwa 2: Ikhtibar al-fasl
p2 = Point2()
p2.set_x(7)
p2.set_y(2)
print("Ihdaathiyat p2: (" + str(p2.get_x()) + ", " + str(p2.get_y()) + ")") 
print("Masafat p2 min al-asl = " + str(p2.distance_from_origin()))

هذه الطريقة تحسب وتُعيد مسافة النقطة من الأصل (0,0). الوسيط (المسمى self) يتم تمريره تلقائيًا من قبل مفسر بايثون عندما تُستدعى الطريقة على مثيل من الفئة.

لا تحتوي هذه الطريقة على معلمات أخرى لأن البيانات الوحيدة التي نحتاج استخدامها في هذه الطريقة هي صفات مثيل الفئة (إحداثيات النقطة) ويمكننا الوصول مباشرة إلى صفات المثيل من داخل طرق الفئة.
لاحظ أن بايثون يملأ الوسيط الأول تلقائيًا بكائن المثيل الذي هو الموضوع الضمني لاستدعاء الطريقة. لذلك، عند استدعاء هذه الطريقة على مثيل من الفئة، لا يجب تمرير أي معطى إلى الطريقة.

untr_comments.content:
This method calculates and returns the distance of the point from the origin (0,0). The argument (named self) is passed in automatically by the interpreter when the method is invoked on an instance of the class.

This method does not have any other parameters because the only data that we need to use in this method are the attribute of the instance of the class (the coordinates of the point) and we can directly access the instance attributes from the methods that are inside the class.

Note that Python automatically fills the first argument in with the instance object that is the implied subject of the method call. Therefore, when this method is invoked on an instance of the class, no parameter must be passed to the method.

untr_comments.content:
This statement calculates and returns the distance of the point from the origin (0,0). To calculate the distance of the point from the origin (0,0), we need to use the Pythagorean Theorem, taking the square root of the sum of the squares of the x and y values.
self is the instance of the class, self.__x is the x-coordinate of the instance, and self.__y is the y-coordinate of the instance. We start the attribute names by two underscore (self.__x and self.__y) to prevent accessing the attributes directly from outside of the class.
Note that we could take square root of a number by raising that number to the power of 0.5. The ** operator is the exponent operator.

untr_comments.content: This statement concatenates the content of the given strings and variables to print the coordinates of p2. To get p2's coordinates, we invoke the method get_x and get_y of p2. Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned value from each of these methods in a variable. We could use the returned value of them directly in the print statement.

We concatenate the content of p2 coordinates with the other strings using the + operator. The coordinates of the point hold integer values and their values can be concatenated with strings only when they're explicitly converted to a string using the str function.
Note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.
Note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined. This string will be printed by the print function and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

untr_comments.content: This statement prints the distance of p2 from the origin to the default standard output stream. To get the distance of p2 from the origin, we invoke the method distance_from_origin of p2. Note that p2 is the implied subject (instance) passed to self. Also, note that this method must be called after the set_x and set_y methods are called.

An error would occur if we call the distance_from_origin method before we call the set_x and set_y methods. Because the class Point2 doesn't have a __init__() method that initialize the coordinates of the point. So by the time p2 is instantiated, the coordinates of p2 are not present. Therefore, We must first call the set_x and set_y methods to set the values of the coordinates.

Note that We concatenate the content of p2 coordinates with the given string using the + operator. The distance from the origin is a number and can be concatenated with strings only when it's explicitly converted to a string using the str function.

Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned value from this method in a variable. We could use the returned value directly in the print statement.
Also, note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.
Note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined. This string will be printed by the print function and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

untr_name: The Class for Representing a Point in the Euclidean Plane (Case 2)
untr_description: Construct a class that represents a point in the Euclidean plane. The class should contain data that represents the point’s integer coordinates (x,y). The point's coordinates could be accessed or changed only through the getter and setter methods. The class should also include a method to calculate and return the point's distance from the origin (0,0).
untr_code:
#Step 1: Define the class
class Point2 :
    #Step 1.1: Declare the method to calculate and return the point's distance from the origin
    def distance_from_origin(self) :
        return (self.__x * self.__x + self.__y * self.__y) ** 0.5
    #Step 1.2: Define the setter and getter methods for the x-coordinate of the point
    def set_x(self, new_x) :
        self.__x = new_x
    def get_x(self) :
        return self.__x
    #Step 1.3: Define the setter and getter methods for the y-coordinate of the point
    def set_y(self, new_y) :
        self.__y = new_y
    def get_y(self) :
        return self.__y
#Step 2: Test the class
p2 = Point2()
p2.set_x(7)
p2.set_y(2)
print("p2 coordinates: (" + str(p2.get_x()) + ", " + str(p2.get_y()) + ")") 
print("Distance of p2 from origin = " + str(p2.distance_from_origin()))
